Good web design San Antonio businesses can count on has to work for someone who knew nothing about the city last month. San Antonio calls itself Military City USA, and a steady share of the people searching for a plumber, a dentist or a dog groomer here arrived recently on military orders, or married someone who did. They have no neighbor to ask yet. Your website is the neighbor.

Dominion Web Design Pro is Maurice Johnson, a Texan writing every page by hand from Big Sandy in East Texas. He researches your trade and your side of town, builds a free demo for your business, and you decide after seeing it. The prices are printed below and paid once.

Military City customers search for everything from scratch

Joint Base San Antonio brings together Fort Sam Houston, Lackland and Randolph. In its 2025 report the Texas Comptroller counted 74,713 direct employees at JBSA, including 33,256 active-duty personnel, and estimated the base population added at least $53 billion to the Texas economy. Lackland is where the Air Force runs its enlisted basic military training, and Fort Sam Houston is the center of Army medical training, home to Brooke Army Medical Center.

For a small business that means a customer base that turns over. Families come in for an assignment, rent or buy, look for a pediatrician, a mechanic, a hair stylist and a church, and some leave again a few years later. The next family starts the search all over. A site that assumes people already know you, already know where you are, or already know what your trade calls things will lose them.

What a new arrival checks first

  • Do you serve the part of town they just moved to?
  • What does a first visit or a service call cost, roughly?
  • Are you open evenings or Saturdays, when they are off duty?
  • Can they call or book with one tap from a phone?

What usually stops them

  • A home page that talks about you and never names a neighborhood
  • Hours that disagree with the Google listing
  • Prices hidden behind "call for a quote" with no range at all
  • Jargon a newcomer to Texas or to your trade does not know

A San Antonio owner, walked through

Picture a typical case: a military spouse who starts a home cleaning business after the family settles on the north side. She has a phone full of before and after photos, a few regulars from the spouses' network, and no time. What she needs from a website is narrow. It should say which areas she cleans, whether she brings supplies, how pricing works for a move-out clean when a family gets new orders, and how to book.

That last point is a real San Antonio detail. Every reassignment season brings people who need a rental cleaned before they hand back the keys. A page written for that one job, in plain words, does more for her than a slideshow ever will. Maurice asks those questions first, then writes the pages around the answers.

San Antonio website design that names the right district

Google says local results weigh relevance, distance and prominence. Distance is the one you cannot argue with, but you can make your location and service area obvious, and that matters in a city of about 1.55 million people, 1,548,422 by the Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate. Somebody in one corner of town is not looking for a shop forty minutes away. These are a few of the places a San Antonio site might name, and what tends to matter in each.

PlaceWhat is thereWhat a page for it should cover
The PearlThe old Pearl Brewery grounds, redeveloped after a 2002 purchase into a walkable district of restaurants, shops, apartments and a weekend farmers marketWalking directions, parking, what you sell, and event or market days
St. Mary's StripBars, food and live music venues along St. Mary's Street in Tobin Hill, just north of downtown and close to the PearlLate hours, the kitchen's closing time, the music calendar
South Texas Medical CenterMore than 900 acres on the northwest side; a 2022 study tied it to more than 86,000 jobsLunch hours, delivery to clinics, child care and services for shift workers
Near the basesFort Sam Houston, Lackland and Randolph, each with its own ring of neighborhoodsWhich gate or side of town you are near, military family questions, evening hours
Stone Oak and the far north sideStone Oak, the first master-planned community in Bexar County, north of Loop 1604 and west of US 281Home services, which ZIP codes you cover, how fast you can come out

Southtown, Broadway and the West Side each deserve the same treatment if you work there. The point is not to list every neighborhood in Bexar County. It is to describe the few you really serve, in words a resident would use. Visitors on the River Walk are a real market for some businesses, but for most owners the steady money comes from people who live here.

What San Antonio website designers should quote you

Searches for "affordable web design San Antonio" and "small business web design San Antonio" come from owners who have seen quotes that wander. Here is ours, plainly. Starter is $497 for five hand-written pages (home, services, about, contact, service area), a contact form that emails every lead, Google Maps and hours, live in 7 to 14 days. Pro is $997 and adds a 10-page site with a photo gallery, lead capture on every page, local SEO with Google Business Profile setup, ten researched city pages and your Google reviews on the site; its AI chat widget is free for 14 days, then $297 a month if you keep it. Agency is $1,997 and starts with keyword research across your whole service area, then a page for each town and service worth having, delivered in waves with the first live inside two weeks, plus custom design. Agency includes setup of an AI phone agent; the agent itself is free for 7 days, then $297 a month for up to 750 minutes, cancel any time.

Hosting, maintenance and updates are included while you keep an AI agent; otherwise they are $49 a month. You own the site. We do not sell page counts: thirty pages that each say something true beat a hundred filler pages, and a plumber who covers four districts well needs four good pages, not forty.

Free help for San Antonio owners before you spend on anything

  • City of San Antonio Economic Development DepartmentRuns small business programs and grants, a Vendor Development Academy, the SBEDA program for city contracting and a Buy Local effort. The city also works with a Small Business Advisory Commission on small business needs.
  • UTSA Small Business Development CenterConfidential one-on-one advising at no cost, plus workshops and training, for San Antonio, Bexar County and the surrounding counties, from an office at UTSA's downtown campus.
  • San Antonio Hispanic Chamber of CommerceDescribes itself as the leading resource and advocate for Hispanic businesses and the Hispanic market, and holds an annual Small Business Expo and awards luncheon. Census figures put San Antonio's Hispanic or Latino population at 64.6%, so this network reaches a large share of local owners.

An SBDC advisor can help you decide what to spend on marketing at all. Our free Site Check will show what an existing site is missing before you change anything.

Common questions

How much do web designers charge in San Antonio?

It depends on how they bill. Some charge by the hour, some quote a project after a meeting, and some rent you a site for a monthly fee that never stops. Our prices are printed: Starter is $497, Pro is $997 and Agency is $1,997, each paid once. After launch, hosting, maintenance and updates cost $49 a month, or nothing extra while you keep an AI agent. Whoever you talk to, ask for the full first-year cost in writing so you can compare fairly.

What should I ask a web designer in San Antonio, TX before hiring?

Ask who will write the words, whether you own the site and the domain when it is done, what you pay every month after launch, and whether you can see something built for your business before you sign. Ask to see how your service area will be described too. A designer who cannot tell you which parts of San Antonio your pages will name has not thought about your customers yet.

Can I keep my website if my military family gets reassigned away from San Antonio?

Yes. You own the finished site outright, and because Maurice already works with every owner remotely, a move changes nothing on our side. If your business moves with you, the pages can be rewritten for the new town. If it stays behind with a partner, the site stays with the business.

Do you build WordPress sites for San Antonio businesses?

We do not sell a particular platform. Every site is hand-built, you own it, and hosting and updates can be handled for you. If you already run WordPress, Shopify or another system and need to stay on it, say so when you ask for the free demo and Maurice will tell you plainly whether it fits.

Can you build an online store for my San Antonio shop?

Online stores with a shopping cart are not part of our packages, and we would rather say that up front than sell you something half-built. Many local shops do well with a site that shows what they carry, their hours and a way to call or order by phone. If you truly need a store, a store platform or a designer who specializes in them is the better fit.
